day.readme: This repo is the source repository for GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform.

day.description: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security
day.readme: Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code. Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the @openai/codex-security CLI and TypeScript SDK. In Codex: choose a security workflow. In a terminal: install the CLI and scan your repository. In automation: use the TypeScript SDK or Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.

day.description: Enable Hermès Watch Faces on any Apple Watch devices
day.readme: Download the IPA from Releases. On your iPhone, open the Watch app and install HermesEnabler2 from My Watch → Apps. Open HermesEnabler2 on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app. Open HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj in Xcode. Select your Apple Watch as the run destination and click Run. Open HermesEnabler2 on your Apple Watch and follow the steps in the app. In Sideloadly, disable Use automatic bundle ID and use a fixed Bundle Identifier.

day.description: The personal finance app for everyone (by everyone)
day.readme: involved: Discord • Website • Issues The Maybe Finance (archived/abandoned repo) team spent most of 2021–2022 building a full-featured personal finance and wealth management app. It even included an “Ask an Advisor” feature that connected users with a real CFP/CFA, all included with your subscription. The business end of things didn't work out, and so they stopped developing the app in mid-2023.

day.description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.
day.readme: The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat. Agentic out of the box, Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams, and MCP. Dynamic workflows, zero setup. Open-source, inside and out, The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in. Multi-protocol, Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. Looking for Qwen Code 1.0 Preview? Get started here.

day.description: LLM Inference Engine for Metal, CUDA and Vulkan.
day.readme: TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the contributor skill before it writes any code. Please use Agent Traffic Control before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes.

day.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
day.readme: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents. Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. In Claude Code these install as plugin commands.

day.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready
day.readme: An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now: by people and the agents working alongside them. Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company, powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day.

day.description: Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
day.readme: A modular, self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers. Choose your models. Bring your agents. Own your infrastructure. From CopilotKit, creators of AG-UI. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c60f07da-8b6d-46eb-a573-17fc1e65a644 Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

day.description: Use Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, VSCode, Pi, and OpenCode (and 6 other harnesses) for free (1.3B+ free tokens) from your terminal, app, IDE, or phone, and now from the browser with native browser sessions (multi-harness + multi-model) like OpenClaw (voice supported + ToS friendly)
day.readme: Independent open-source project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic. Route any supported harness to models from any supported provider. 12 supported harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Cline, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, Grok Build, Muse Code, Aider, Antigravity CLI, or VS Code Chat. Preserved native streaming, tool use, and interleaved thinking for maximum performance. For Claude Code, route Fable, Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku to supported models.

A few options to get llama.cpp installed on your machine: Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions Run with Docker - see our Docker documentation Download pre-built binaries from the releases page Build from source by cloning this repository - check out our build guide Built-in web UI against llama serve The main goal of llama.cpp is to enable LLM (and VLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware - locally and in the cloud.

week.readme: Skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to improve performance on specialized tasks. Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks.

week.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use
week.readme: The open-source Grok Bot alternative: your own team of AI bots, in a chat app. OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative: an independent project inspired by Grok Bot, and the open-source alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI dots and Cue by Manus, bring-your-own-agent, local-first, on the models you already have. Also known as MausBot; formerly OpenGrokBot. Not affiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI or Manus.

week.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
week.readme: Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call.

week.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
week.readme: Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API.

week.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
week.readme: A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness. The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

week.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
week.readme: Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library.

week.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
week.readme: My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

week.description: Code at the speed of thought – Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.
week.readme: Welcome to Zed, a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter. On macOS, Linux, and Windows you can download Zed directly or install Zed via your local package manager (macOS/Linux/Windows). Other platforms are not yet available: See CONTRIBUTING.md for ways you can contribute to Zed. Also... we're hiring! Check out our jobs page for open roles. Zed source code is licensed primarily under GPL-3.0-or-later, with Apache-2.0 components where marked.

week.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
week.readme: MuJoCo stands for Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. It is a general purpose physics engine that aims to facilitate research and development in robotics, biomechanics, graphics and animation, machine learning, and other areas which demand fast and accurate simulation of articulated structures interacting with their environment. This repository is maintained by Google DeepMind. MuJoCo has a C API and is intended for researchers and developers.

week.readme: This repository contains Agent Skills for Google products and technologies, including Google Cloud. When prompted, select specific skills or all skills, the target agents to configure, and the installation scope (project or global). week.description: 🕷️ The BEST Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl! Don't be shy, join here: https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ and follow here for daily tips and tricks: https://x.com/Scrapling_dev

Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill.

month.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
month.readme: See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level. Join the Reverse Engineering Community See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites.

month.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
month.readme: Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it. Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together. Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

month.description: The best way to control Claude Code, Codex and more from any computer or phone
month.readme: The open-source control plane for coding agents. T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. Every agent in one place.

Cowork lets you set the goal and Claude delivers finished, professional work. Plugins let you go further: tell Claude how you like work done, which tools and data to pull from, how to handle critical workflows, and what slash commands to expose, so your team gets better and more consistent outcomes.

new.description: A Native Recompilation Of The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Nintendo Switch 2 Remake
new.readme: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator. Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows or Linux program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game. Discord: https://discord.gg/rexed Experimental. Most testing so far has been around the start of the game.

Selecting United States for Region Code sets RegionCode to LL and keeps the sales-region suffix. You can also choose China (Mainland), Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan or the United Kingdom. new.readme: Your own Switch games, running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Game code is rewritten to native ARM64 and runs directly on the device's processor, with graphics going straight to Metal. Your whole library lives in one app, and a few clicks in the Mac or Windows launcher take a game from import to play. The game's own ARM64 code is rewritten at build time and then runs directly on the processor in your iPhone, iPad or Mac. There is no CPU emulator in between.

new.description: Entire MacOS running in your terminal.
new.readme: A separate macOS desktop for computer-use agents, viewed and controlled from a terminal. terminal-mac is an early release candidate for Apple silicon. Apple Virtualization runs a real macOS guest. A bundled helper inside that guest captures its screen and posts input events. A terminal viewer streams that screen using Kitty or iTerm2 graphics. Agent commands use the same helper without moving the physical Mac's pointer or changing its clipboard.

new.description: A GPU task manager for Windows, Linux, and WSL: per-process VRAM, GPU activity, and LLM model/KV-cache insights (Windows AMD and NVIDIA).
new.readme: An htop for what's inside your GPU, not just how full it is. Windows + NVIDIA/AMD, with Linux and WSL support (NVIDIA everywhere, AMD and Intel on native Linux; see Linux and WSL) and macOS on Apple Silicon (see macOS). A terminal UI that connects per-process GPU memory and engine activity with loaded runtimes, model files, and Task Manager says "15 GB used." This tries to answer: by what? Model weights? KV cache? Your browser? The desktop compositor? And why is so much GPU memory in system RAM?

new.description: 3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.
new.readme: 3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs. sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs: profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and assemblies, over Blender's bpy. A program says how a shape is made, part by part and in its own words, so a model writes it in a few hundred tokens How it is measured, part by part Short. A part takes 2 to 6× fewer tokens than the same part in Blender Python, CadQuery or FeatureScript (details). The whole API fits in a prompt, about 3,600 tokens (the API).

items.title: Cloud coding agents can test AWS changes in sandboxes that hold no AWS credentials
items.connection: Cline's cloud sandboxes clone a repo and start an agent, and Amazon's CC0 AWS emulator can be baked into that sandbox so the agent exercises cloud code without a real account.
items.context: security teams resist putting long-lived cloud credentials in places agents run unattended
chain: Amazon publishes an AWS emulator under CC0, and Cline can already run long agent tasks in cloud sandboxes.
A team adds the emulator to the sandbox image, so the agent's tests hit a local AWS stand-in instead of a live account.
No AWS keys need to live in the sandbox, so the security review that blocks cloud agent runs gets much shorter.
Long unattended runs on infrastructure code become routine, and real-account testing shrinks to a final, human-gated stage.
items.who: Platform and DevOps teams benefit. Engineering orgs paying for Cline cloud tasks and dev AWS accounts would pay for a hardened sandbox template.
items.variable: number of agent environments holding live cloud credentials
items.versus: Doing nothing means either no cloud agent runs on AWS code or keys in sandboxes, and paid sandbox products do not ship a vendor-published AWS stand-in.
items.smallest_test: Take one repo with AWS deployment tests, run them in a Cline cloud sandbox against the emulator, and count success if at least 80% of the tests that pass on a real dev account also pass there with zero credentials present.
items.disconfirm: The emulator lacks the services the repo uses, or its behavior differs enough that most emulator passes fail on the real account.

items.title: Robot startups can check training data coverage for a client task before quoting
items.connection: DINOv3 frozen image features can index RoboCap-10k's 10,000 hours of egocentric work video, so a handful of client clips can retrieve similar real-work segments across 21 industries.
items.context: robot pilots often fail on tasks with too little relevant training data
chain: RoboCap-10k opens 10,000 hours of paid work video across 21 industries, and a DINOv3 ViT-L/16 checkpoint is available for feature extraction.
A startup embeds sampled frames once, then embeds a few clips a prospect films of their own task and retrieves the nearest segments.
The amount of close matching footage becomes a quick proxy for whether open data can support that task.
Sales teams quote only on tasks with coverage, and data collection budgets go to the gaps the search exposes.
items.who: Robotics startups and automation consultants benefit. Their prospects, such as logistics or food plants, effectively pay through better scoped pilots.
items.variable: share of quoted pilots that reach a working demo
items.versus: Today scoping relies on gut feel or costly custom filming, and no existing product searches open work video against a client's own clips.
items.smallest_test: Embed a slice of the dataset, query with clips of three known tasks and one unrelated task, and count success if a person rates at least 7 of the top 10 hits as the same task for the three known ones and few for the unrelated one.
items.disconfirm: Retrieval returns visually similar scenes, like the same lighting or setting, rather than the same work action.

items.title: Call centers can run offline voice role-play trainers that stay responsive through long sessions
items.connection: Handy does offline speech to text, ZONOS3-Mini speaks replies without a hosted API, and TensorFold's history reuse keeps follow-ups fast as a practice call grows long.
items.context: per-minute hosted voice APIs get expensive for daily training across many seats

items.variable: practice hours per new agent before first live call
items.versus: Hosted voice bots charge per minute and send audio offsite, and without history reuse a local loop stalls badly as the call grows.
items.smallest_test: Run a scripted role-play on one Mac until history passes 34k tokens and count success if every reply starts speaking within 3 seconds of the trainee finishing.
items.disconfirm: ZONOS3-Mini quality or license rules it out, or the TensorFold speedup does not appear when transcribed turns are appended.

items.disconfirm: Similarity scores do not track designer judgment, or the Metal speedup does not reproduce on the agency's own Macs.

items.body: Teams can pair Runway's Apache 2.0 Praxis-1, which takes LoRA fine-tuning and serves in vLLM-Omni down to Jetson Thor, with RoboCap-10k's 10,000 hours of real work video from 21 industries. That lowers the cost of trying robot policies on the kind of data they usually lack. Praxis-1's 80.0% on SimplerEnv is a simulation result, and no models trained on RoboCap-10k are reported yet.
